items.label: MA-AG civil: Safe Home Security, Security Systems, Inc., Safe Home Monitoring, Inc. and National Protective Services, Inc.
items.detail: Suffolk Superior Court consent judgment over deceptive auto renewal contracts and illegal debt collection; date is the announcement date. Total is $1.8 million paid plus $4.7 million in debt waived, ordered of the company, its sister companies and CEO David G. Roman, jointly and severally (judgment paragraph 29, with Mr. Roman's personal guaranty in paragraph 30); no defendant has a stated share. Cash-only rule applied 2026-10-11: amount changed from 6,500,000 to 1,800,000; the part not counted is listed in data/manual/excluded-amounts.csv as xa-010. | Not counted in the total. Shared total, split not stated by the source: counted for no company, kept in gross (overlap group shared-ma-ag-2023-safe-home-security; listed under Amounts not counted).

excluded_amounts.defendant: Safe Home Security, Security Systems, Inc., Safe Home Monitoring, Inc. and National Protective Services, Inc.
excluded_amounts.reason: Release: "a $6.5 million settlement, including $4.7 million in debt relief". Counted: the $1.8 million paid. Not counted: the waived debt. Update 2026-10-11 (shared total): the $1.8 million is itself one total that the filed judgment (https://www.mass.gov/doc/commonwealth-v-safe-home-security-consent-judgment/download, paragraphs 29 and 30) has the corporate defendants and CEO David Roman pay jointly and severally, with his personal guaranty and no share stated for any defendant, so it is counted for no company (overlap group shared-ma-ag-2023-safe-home-security, data/manual/shared-allocations.csv). The judgment's suspended penalty of $1,000,000, payable on default (paragraph 32), is conditional and not counted.
